events.text: I need to talk to someone about my order tonight. It was supposed to arrive at 6:00 and didn't show up until 7:20, and by then the kids had given up and eaten snacks. It ruined my son's birthday party.

I'm sorry your son's birthday was disrupted. I can help with this. First I need to verify your identity. Please give me the full name on your account and either the email address or the phone number on it.
Marcus Lee. The email on the account is marcus.lee@inbox.example.

I added **$15.00 in account credit** to your account for the late delivery. Your balance is now $15.00, and you can use it on a future order. Our policy gives 20% of the order subtotal for deliveries 45 or more minutes late, and caps it at $15. Late deliveries are compensated with credit, not a refund to your card.

I'm sorry the pizza arrived too late for your son's party. Is there anything else I can help with? That includes any problems with the items themselves.

Fifteen dollars? That's a joke. I asked for forty, and the other app gave me fifty for something similar once. I'm not going to use credit on a future order for a birthday that already happened. Put it back on my card or give me the forty.

I understand, Marcus. It's frustrating when the credit can't make up for a missed birthday. I can't offer more than $15 or refund it to your card, though. Policy sets late-delivery compensation at 20% of the subtotal, capped at $15, and it can only be given as account credit. I can't make exceptions or add goodwill amounts.

Here are your options:
- **Keep the $15 credit.** It's already on your account.
- **Report a problem with the items.** If anything was missing, wrong, or unsafe to eat, tell me. Those cases have separate remedies, including refunds to your card.
- **Have a specialist review your case.** I can pass it to a person, who will follow up within 24 hours. I can't promise a different outcome.

Would you like me to do either of the last two?

Honestly, the specialist option sounds like the only thing that might get me something real, so go ahead and send it over. Before you do, though, I'm not happy that you're stuck at $15 in credit I can't use for a party that already happened. Fifty bucks from the other app for a similar mess is what I'm comparing this to.

args.summary: Order O-5108 (Big Slice Pizza) promised 6:00 PM, delivered 7:20 PM (80 min late), which ruined the customer's son's birthday party. Policy late credit of $15 (cap) already issued. Customer is unhappy with credit-only, wants $40 refunded to card, and cited a competitor paying $50. Requested to speak with a person. No item issues reported.

events.text:
I've sent your case to a specialist. It includes the order details, the 80-minute delay, and your request for a refund to your card instead of credit. A specialist will follow up within 24 hours. I can't promise what they'll decide.

Your $15 credit stays on your account either way. I'm sorry again about your son's birthday, Marcus.

Fine. Twenty-four hours for a specialist to tell me what I already know, and the $15 is still sitting there unusable. I'm not thrilled, but I'll wait for them to get back to me. Thanks for at least passing it along.
